subject: Clarify: prompt/output PII storage, erasure options, and region for trial
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@medigo.io>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medigo.io>
Date: 2026-06-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + three asks on PII / retention / residency

Alice — thanks for the call earlier. Quick written recap and the three things I promised to confirm so legal and security can sign off for the trial. Attaching a short FAQ and a draft SoW.

TL;DR (please confirm):
- What we store: prompt text and model outputs are not persisted to long-term storage by default; we retain short operational logs.
- Retention options: customer-configurable TTL (default 30 days), option for immediate erase on demand for trial tenants.
- Residency: trial can be provisioned in us-east-1; logs and any persisted artifacts can be restricted to that region.

Actions / ask from you:
1) Confirm whether Medigo needs a contract addendum for per-tenant erasure (legal requested this).
2) Confirm desired TTL for the trial tenant (default 30 days vs. 0 days/ephemeral).
3) Tell us whether audit logs should include verbatim prompts or redacted metadata only.

Attachments: PII-handling-FAQ.pdf; SoW-draft.docx (high level SOW for 3-week POC).

Next steps: I’ll loop in Ben (solutions) and Marissa (security) to answer the technical specifics and share a proposed trial tenant configuration. Can we aim to land this by end of next week?

Thanks — Hannah

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@medigo.io>

Date: 2026-06-03T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + three asks on PII / retention / residency

Thanks, Hannah — good summary. A few clarifying questions from our side (legal + infra):

1) When you say "not persisted to long-term storage by default," do you mean the raw prompt text is never written to S3 or equivalent buckets, or it's stored for X hours/days for debugging? We have compliance that forbids any long-term storage of PHI.

2) For per-tenant TTL: can we set TTL=0 for the trial (immediate deletion after processing) and still retain the troubleshooting logs necessary if we run into issues? Or is that mutually exclusive?

3) Audit logs: our security team wants to be able to show request/response hashes (not plaintext) for audit — is there an automatic hashing option or would we need to store encrypted copies?

4) Regional assurance: you mentioned us-east-1. Does that also mean encryption keys and audit logs remain in-region? If keys are customer-managed, can we provide our KMS?

If you can answer these at a high level, we’ll escalate to legal. We’d also like the SoW before our procurement kickoff (legal wants to see the erasure obligations in writing).

— Alice

Head of Product, Medigo Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@medigo.io>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-03T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick recap + three asks on PII / retention / residency

Hi Alice — quick answers to your four bullets, from the engineering/security side. Keeping it concrete so legal has language to work with. Attaching a short architecture figure and the retention SLA.

1) Raw prompts: By default, Redwood routes prompts through an ephemeral in-memory pipeline. For hosted tenants we keep operational trace logs for 0–72 hours (configurable) which may include a hashed pointer to the prompt. Raw prompt text is not persisted to durable object storage (S3/GCS) unless the customer explicitly enables "persist prompts" for debugging. In other words: long-term storage of plaintext PHI is opt-in only.

2) TTL=0 / immediate deletion: We support a trial profile that sets request TTL to 0 for persisted artifacts. If TTL=0 is selected, automated debugging traces that include plaintext are disabled. We can still capture anonymized traces and request/response digests (hashes) to diagnose issues. If you need reversible debugging, that requires explicit opt-in and a documented sign-off.

3) Audit hashes: We provide an automatic hashing layer that computes request/response digests (SHA-256) and stores the digest in the audit log. Digests do not contain plaintext and are sufficient for integrity verification during audits. If you need to map a digest back to content, that only happens if the customer enabled prompt persistence and provides the key to correlate — otherwise digest -> content mapping is not stored.

4) Region & KMS: Trial tenants can be provisioned in us-east-1 and all long-term artifacts (if any) will be scoped to that region. We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for encryption-at-rest. Audit logs are written to a region-limited logging service; we can restrict log replication to the same region for the trial.

Compliance notes: We have a SOC 2 Type II report and can provide a redacted copy to legal; for PHI-specific flows we recommend the TTL=0 trial configuration + hashed audit logs.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll update the SoW draft with the TTL=0 trial profile language and a brief clause describing hashing-only audit logs.
- Marissa, can you add an explicit erasure SLA paragraph and sample contract language for legal?

If that sounds good I’ll push updated docs by end of day.

Ben Carter
